card.name: Shell prompts before admin commands
card.fires_on: The shell prompt symbol (% or /#) or nearby punctuation just before a sysadmin command in Unix tutorials, and also file-listing fields like owner names. Also weakly the digit 9 inside years like 1791 and 1798.

modes.label: Shell prompt
modes.description: The % or /# prompt marker right before a typed sudo or admin command.
modes.example: This command will enable ACLs on the boot volume. <<%>> sudo /usr/sbin/fsaclctl -

modes.label: File listing fields
modes.description: A link count or owner name inside an ls-style permissions line.

modes.label: Digit in 1790s year
modes.description: The digit 9 in a year like 1791 or 1798 in local history text.

card.writes: It suppresses admin and administration words, so it steers away from administrative terms.
